proposals: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish a searchable register of every Section 3(1) and Section 6(1) notice under the 1962 Right of User Act, with S.O. number, pipeline, operator, fluid, state, district and village, so the roughly 700 notices can be traced to projects without reconstructing them from secondary write-ups.

PNGRB should publish its pipeline data-bank as a dated, machine-readable series with authorised, operational and under-construction lengths for each pipeline, so totals such as 33,500, 33,764 and 34,233 km can be reconciled snapshot by snapshot.

GAIL should publish, for each pipeline under construction, the original and every revised completion date with the stated reason, so slippage on KKBMPL, the Srikakulam–Angul spur and JHBDPL can be tracked from the company rather than from conflicting trade reports.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish, for each Section 3(1) notice, the number of objections received in the 21-day window and how they were disposed of, so the right-of-user process can be assessed on its record and not only on its design.

The Ministry of Environment should show on PARIVESH the current stage and outstanding conditions of the forest clearance for the 56 km stretch of the Srikakulam–Angul spur line, so the cause of its revised completion date can be followed from the clearance record itself.
